title: 953 Foreign Business Owners Have Left Japan in 2026
paragraphs: A growing number of foreign business owners are leaving Japan after the country introduced stricter rules for business visas.

According to data from Japan's Immigration Services Agency, 953 people holding a "business manager" visa left Japan between January and June 2026 without completing the steps needed to return. This means their stay in Japan effectively ended. The number is about 3.9 times higher than in the same period of 2025.

The business manager visa allows foreign people to start or run a company in Japan. In October 2025, the government made the rules for this visa much stricter. Before the change, applicants needed 5 million yen in capital to start a business. Now, they need at least 30 million yen. In addition, a business must have at least one full-time employee who meets certain conditions, and either the business owner or that employee must be able to speak Japanese at a fairly high level. The government is also checking business plans more carefully.
The government said the changes were needed because some foreign people were using "shell companies," which are businesses that exist only on paper, to get visas.

The new rules seem to have had a very big effect. New applications for the visa reportedly fell from about 1,700 a month to around 70 after the change. People who already hold the visa have three years to meet the new conditions, but some say they have had trouble renewing their visas.

Some foreign business owners say the new rules are unfair. Ray Hoe, who bought an old Japanese-style inn in Toyama to turn into a hotel, was told to leave the country after his visa renewal was refused. He moved to Singapore in July. He said he did not think the changes had been well thought through.
